processing: Ceylon black tea, fully oxidised and made in the estates' factories; part of the company's output is grown organically, some of it biodynamically.
harvest_season: Year-round, as across Sri Lanka's hills. Western high-grown teas are generally best in the dry months early in the year.
appearance_dry: Dark, well-made leaf in the standard Ceylon grades, as is usual for the district.
appearance_liquor: Clear reddish-amber, as is typical of western high-grown Ceylon.
appearance_wet: Coppery-brown pieces or open leaf, depending on the grade.
taste_profile: Few independent notes tie down this tea. Western high-grown Ceylon usually pours brisk and clean with a gentle floral lift.

brewing.notes: Western style. Works with or without milk; shorten the steep for broken grades.

vintage_note: Sold by estate and grade, either through auction or in the company's own packs, not by year. Like most Ceylon black tea it is best within a year or two. Organic lots are labelled and certified separately.
description:
Bogawantalawa is both a place and a name on the packet: a valley in Sri Lanka's central hills, around a town at about 1,514 m, and the company Bogawantalawa Tea Estates PLC, which grows tea there. The company calls it the Golden Valley of Ceylon Tea, which is its own phrase and best read as such.

The teas are ordinary-process Ceylon blacks. The more unusual side is the organic line launched in 2023 and biodynamic methods on the company's Norwood fields, with Rainforest Alliance and USDA organic among its listed accreditations.

This is hill-country tea, and the valley is sometimes grouped with Dimbula. As with other western high-grown teas, expect a brisk, clean cup, with more lift in the dry months.

When buying, check which estate or division a pack names, because Bogawantalawa on the label may mean the company as much as a single garden.
history:
The company's own account starts in 1869, with Scottish planters arriving in the valley, and says its Tientsin division grew from seedlings brought from a Chinese village more than 150 years ago. Both are the company's claims.

The corporate record is clearer: incorporated in 1992 as Bogawantalawa Plantations Limited, renamed Bogawantalawa Tea Estates PLC in April 2008, with BPL Teas set up as its marketing arm in 1997.
